# ===== FUNCTION: Database.transaction() =====
    # ID: F0425 · method · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/db.py:92-102
    # ROLE: Run several statements atomically (all succeed or none), e.g. "insert execution record + set status executed".
    # INPUTS:
    #   statements: list[tuple[str, tuple]] -> [(sql, params), ...].
    # OUTPUT:
    #   None.
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0352 _PostgresDb.run() (calls)
    #   <- F0358 Store.audit() (calls)
    #   <- F0423 Database.execute() (calls)
    #   <- F0424 Database.executemany() (calls)
    #   <- F0426 Database.atomic() (calls)
    #   <- F0428 Database._script() (calls)
    #   <- F0535 promote() (calls)
    #   <- F0765 KnowledgeBase.ingest_dir() (calls)
    #   <- F0340 Service.record_sap_execution() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0420 Database._sql() (calls)
    def transaction(self, statements: list[tuple[str, tuple]]) -> None:
        """Run several statements atomically (all or nothing)."""
        if self.dialect == "sqlite":
            with self._lock, self._conn:
                # Tuple unpacking in the for loop: each item is (sql, params).
                for sql, params in statements:
                    self._conn.execute(sql, params)
            return
        with self._pool.connection() as conn, conn.transaction():
            # Transaction-scoped advisory lock 8817001: serialises these multi-statement writes across API workers.
            conn.execute("select pg_advisory_xact_lock(8817001)")
            for sql, params in statements:
                conn.execute(self._sql(sql), params)

# ===== FUNCTION: Database.atomic() =====
    # ID: F0426 · method · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/db.py:104-117
    # ROLE: Run fn(q) inside ONE transaction holding an exclusive lock, for read-then-write logic (audit chain, status changes).
    # INPUTS:
    #   fn: callable      -> function receiving q(sql, params=()); q returns rows for SELECT, rowcount otherwise.
    #   lock_id: int      -> PostgreSQL advisory lock number (8817002 default; 8817003 for the audit chain).
    # OUTPUT:
    #   whatever fn returns (e.g. True/False "was the row changed").
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0779 Security.audit() (calls)
    #   <- F0337 Service.review() (calls)
    #   <- F0341 Service.reconcile() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0425 Database.transaction() (calls)
    #   -> F0427 Database.atomic.q() (references)
    def atomic(self, fn, lock_id: int = 8817002):
        """Run fn(q) inside one transaction holding an exclusive lock; q(sql, params) returns rows. For read-then-write logic
        such as the audit hash chain or status transitions, so concurrent requests cannot interleave."""
        if self.dialect == "sqlite":
            with self._lock, self._conn:
                # Inline lambda as q: SELECT -> fetchall(), anything else -> rowcount. The Python RLock provides exclusivity.
                return fn(lambda sql, params=(): self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall()
                          if sql.lstrip().lower().startswith("select") else self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).rowcount)
        with self._pool.connection() as conn, conn.transaction():
            # Other transactions asking for the same lock id wait until this transaction commits.
            conn.execute("select pg_advisory_xact_lock(%s)", (lock_id,))

            # ===== FUNCTION: Database.atomic.q() =====
            # ID: F0427 · nested · used
            # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/db.py:114-116
            # ROLE: The q() helper for PostgreSQL: same contract as the SQLite lambda above.
            # INPUTS:
            #   sql: str, params: tuple -> statement + values.
            # OUTPUT:
            #   list[dict] for SELECT, int rowcount otherwise.
            # CALLED BY:
            #   <- F0426 Database.atomic() (references)
            # CALLS:
            #   -> F0420 Database._sql() (calls)
            def q(sql, params=()):
                cur = conn.execute(self._sql(sql), tuple(params))
                return cur.fetchall() if sql.lstrip().lower().startswith("select") else cur.rowcount
            return fn(q)

# ===== FUNCTION: Database._script() =====
    # ID: F0428 · method · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/db.py:119-129
    # ROLE: Execute a multi-statement SQL script (used by migrations).
    # INPUTS:
    #   script: str -> the content of a .sql file.
    # OUTPUT:
    #   None.
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0429 Database.migrate() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0425 Database.transaction() (calls)
    def _script(self, script: str) -> None:
        if self.dialect == "sqlite":
            with self._lock:
                # executescript runs every ";"-separated statement.
                self._conn.executescript(script)
            return
        # Strip full-line comments first: a ';' inside a comment must not split a statement.
        code = "\n".join(line for line in script.splitlines() if not line.strip().startswith("--"))
        with self._pool.connection() as conn, conn.transaction():
            # Lock 8817000: two API containers starting together cannot run the same migration twice.
            conn.execute("select pg_advisory_xact_lock(8817000)")
            # Split on ";", strip whitespace, filter(None, ...) drops empty strings.
            for statement in filter(None, (s.strip() for s in code.split(";"))):
                conn.execute(statement)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ migrations
    # ===== FUNCTION: Database.migrate() =====
    # ID: F0429 · method · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/db.py:132-145
    # ROLE: Apply, in file-name order, every migration not yet recorded in schema_migrations.
    # INPUTS:
    #   self -> the database.
    # OUTPUT:
    #   list[str] -> versions applied by this call (e.g. ["0001_core", "0002_pgvector.postgres"]).
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0112 create_app() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0428 Database._script() (calls)
    #   -> F0421 Database.query() (calls)
    #   -> F0423 Database.execute() (calls)
    #   -> F0416 now_iso() (calls)
    def migrate(self) -> list[str]:
        # Bookkeeping table: one row per applied migration.
        self._script("create table if not exists schema_migrations (version text primary key, applied_at text not null)")
        # Set comprehension of the versions already applied.
        applied = {r["version"] for r in self.query("select version from schema_migrations")}
        done = []
        # sorted(): 0001_... before 0002_...; glob("*.sql") lists the migration files.
        for path in sorted(MIGRATIONS.glob("*.sql")):
            # path.stem = file name without the last extension ("0002_pgvector.postgres").
            version = path.stem
            if version in applied:
                continue
            # PostgreSQL-only migrations (pgvector) are skipped on SQLite.
            if path.stem.endswith(".postgres") and self.dialect != "postgres":
                continue
            self._script(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.execute("insert into schema_migrations(version, applied_at) values(?, ?)", (version, now_iso()))
            done.append(version)
        return done

# ===== FUNCTION: load() =====
# ID: F0432 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/fixtures.py:101-267
# ROLE: Load the whole synthetic SAP snapshot into the database (idempotent: existing primary keys are kept); optionally wipe first.
# INPUTS:
#   db: Database             -> target database.
#   keys: dict | None        -> real API keys by slot (override DEFAULT_KEYS; only their hashes are stored).
#   reset: bool              -> delete all rows of the listed tables first (tests).
# OUTPUT:
#   dict -> row counts per table for the main tenant (products, materials, inventory_batches, purchase_orders, ...).
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0112 create_app() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0418 Database (references)
#   -> F0416 now_iso() (calls)
#   -> F0423 Database.execute() (calls)
#   -> F0433 load.upsert() (calls)
#   -> F0430 key_hash() (calls)
#   -> F0424 Database.executemany() (calls)
#   -> F0431 _d() (calls)
#   -> F0422 Database.one() (calls)
def load(db: Database, keys: dict[str, str] | None = None, reset: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Load the synthetic fixtures (idempotent: rows are replaced by primary key). Returns counts per table."""
    # Merge: configured keys win over the dev defaults.
    keys = {**DEFAULT_KEYS, **(keys or {})}
    # Fixed seed -> the same "random" quantities on every machine and every run (reproducible tests and demos).
    rng = random.Random(20261021)
    t, now = TENANT, now_iso()
    if reset:
        # Child tables first, then parents (foreign keys).
        for table in ("rag_chunks", "rag_documents", "retraining_requests", "model_versions", "learning_records", "observed_outcomes",
                      "sap_execution_refs", "human_decisions", "recommendations", "agent_runs", "transport_lanes", "sales_history",
                      "purchase_orders", "supplier_items", "suppliers", "production_orders", "inventory_batches", "bom_components",
                      "materials", "products", "warehouses", "sap_snapshots", "role_assignments", "users", "tenants", "audit_events"):
            db.execute(f"delete from {table}")  # noqa: S608 - fixed table list

    # ===== FUNCTION: load.upsert() =====
    # ID: F0433 · nested · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/fixtures.py:113-119
    # ROLE: Insert rows, ignoring those whose primary key already exists (dialect-specific "insert or ignore").
    # INPUTS:
    #   table: str, cols: tuple of column names, rows: list of value tuples.
    # OUTPUT:
    #   None.
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0432 load() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0424 Database.executemany() (calls)
    def upsert(table: str, cols: tuple, rows: list[tuple]) -> None:
        # "?,?,?" with one "?" per column ("?" * 3 = "???", joined with commas).
        placeholders = ",".join("?" * len(cols))
        if db.dialect == "postgres":
            sql = f"insert into {table}({','.join(cols)}) values({placeholders}) on conflict do nothing"  # noqa: S608
        else:
            sql = f"insert or ignore into {table}({','.join(cols)}) values({placeholders})"  # noqa: S608
        db.executemany(sql, rows)

    upsert("tenants", ("id", "name", "industry", "synthetic", "industry_sharing_enabled", "created_at"),
           [(t, "Belleva Cosmetics (synthetic)", "cosmetics", 1, 0, now), (OTHER_TENANT, "Northwind Pharma (synthetic)", "pharmaceutical", 1, 0, now)])
    # Users: the key HASH is stored, never the key. `_` ignores the roles element of the tuple here.
    upsert("users", ("id", "tenant_id", "name", "email", "api_key_hash", "active", "created_at"),
           [(uid, t, name, f"{uid}@belleva.example", key_hash(keys[slot]), 1, now) for slot, uid, name, _ in USERS]
           + [("u-other-tenant", OTHER_TENANT, "Northwind planner (fictional)", "planner@northwind.example", key_hash(keys["other_tenant"]), 1, now)])
    # Key rotation: the configured keys always win over hashes stored by an earlier start (e.g. dev keys).
    db.executemany("update users set api_key_hash=? where id=?",
                   [(key_hash(keys[slot]), uid) for slot, uid, _, _ in USERS] + [(key_hash(keys["other_tenant"]), "u-other-tenant")])
    # Nested comprehension: one role_assignments row per (user, role).
    upsert("role_assignments", ("user_id", "tenant_id", "role"),
           [(uid, t, role) for _, uid, _, roles in USERS for role in roles]
           + [("u-other-tenant", OTHER_TENANT, "planner"), ("u-other-tenant", OTHER_TENANT, "supply_chain_director")])
    # The snapshot record: provenance says clearly that this is NOT real SAP data.
    upsert("sap_snapshots", ("id", "tenant_id", "source_system", "extracted_at", "as_of_date", "status", "synthetic", "provenance"),
           [(SNAPSHOT_ID, t, "S4HANA-SYNTHETIC", "2026-10-21T06:00:00+00:00", BUSINESS_DATE.isoformat(), "valid", 1,
             "Synthetic fixture generated by backend/scinsight/fixtures.py (seed 20261021); not real SAP data."),
            ("SAP-SYN-NW-2026-10-01", OTHER_TENANT, "S4HANA-SYNTHETIC", "2026-10-01T06:00:00+00:00", "2026-10-01", "valid", 1, "Synthetic second tenant")])
    # (t, *loc) unpacks the location tuple after the tenant id.
    upsert("warehouses", ("tenant_id", "code", "name", "kind", "region", "city", "target_cover_days"), [(t, *loc) for loc in LOCATIONS]
           + [(OTHER_TENANT, "WH-X", "Northwind DC (synthetic)", "warehouse", "North", "Oslo", 21)])
    upsert("products", ("tenant_id", "sku", "name", "category", "uom", "shelf_life_days", "unit_cost_eur"),
           [(t, sku, name, cat, "EA", life, cost) for sku, name, cat, life, cost in PRODUCTS]
           + [(OTHER_TENANT, "SUN-SPF50-100", "Northwind sunscreen (synthetic)", "suncare", "EA", 730, 4.0)])
    upsert("materials", ("tenant_id", "material_id", "name", "uom", "unit_cost_eur", "critical"), [(t, *m) for m in MATERIALS])

    # ---- BOMs: SER-VITC-30 v2 approved (scenario 1); v3 is a DRAFT (invalid for planning); SER-RETI-30 has a unit mismatch.
    bom = [(t, "SER-VITC-30", "v2", m, q, u, s, "2026-01-01", None, "approved") for m, q, u, s in [
        ("PUMP-DISP-24", 1, "EA", 0), ("BTL-GLS-30", 1, "EA", 0.5), ("SER-BASE-VC", 0.031, "KG", 2.0), ("CAP-PUMP-OVR", 1, "EA", 0), ("CRT-SER-30", 1, "EA", 0)]]
    bom += [(t, "SER-VITC-30", "v3", "PUMP-DISP-24", 1, "EA", 0, "2026-12-01", None, "draft")]
    bom += [(t, "SER-VITC-30", "v1", "PUMP-DISP-24", 1, "EA", 0, "2025-01-01", "2025-12-31", "approved")]  # expired version
    bom += [(t, "SUN-SPF50-100", "v1", m, q, u, s, "2025-06-01", None, "approved") for m, q, u, s in [
        ("TUB-SUN-100", 1, "EA", 0.5), ("SUN-BASE-50", 0.102, "KG", 1.5), ("LBL-GEN", 1, "EA", 1.0)]]
    bom += [(t, "SER-RETI-30", "v1", "SER-BASE-VC", 30, "ML", 2.0, "2026-01-01", None, "approved"),  # ML vs KG stock: unit mismatch
            (t, "SER-RETI-30", "v1", "PUMP-DISP-24", 1, "EA", 0, "2026-01-01", None, "approved")]
    bom += [(t, "CRM-HYDR-50", "v1", m, q, u, s, "2025-06-01", None, "approved") for m, q, u, s in [
        ("JAR-CRM-50", 1, "EA", 0.5), ("CRM-BASE-HY", 0.052, "KG", 1.5), ("LBL-GEN", 1, "EA", 1.0)]]
    upsert("bom_components", ("tenant_id", "sku", "bom_version", "material_id", "qty_per_unit", "uom", "scrap_pct", "valid_from", "valid_to", "status"), bom)

    # ---- inventory batches
    inv = [  # batch, location, item, type, qty, uom, status, expiry, reserved_for
        ("P-REL-01", "FAC-1", "PUMP-DISP-24", "material", 20000, "EA", "released", None, None),
        ("P-REL-02", "FAC-1", "PUMP-DISP-24", "material", 10000, "EA", "released", None, None),
        ("P-BLK-03", "FAC-1", "PUMP-DISP-24", "material", 4000, "EA", "blocked", None, None),
        ("B-GLS-01", "FAC-1", "BTL-GLS-30", "material", 60000, "EA", "released", None, None),
        ("SB-VC-01", "FAC-1", "SER-BASE-VC", "material", 1800, "KG", "released", "2027-03-31", None),
        ("SB-VC-02", "FAC-1", "SER-BASE-VC", "material", 150, "KG", "released", "2026-10-10", None),  # expired base
        ("CAP-01", "FAC-1", "CAP-PUMP-OVR", "material", 55000, "EA", "released", None, None),
        ("CRT-01", "FAC-1", "CRT-SER-30", "material", 52000, "EA", "released", None, None),
        ("TUB-01", "FAC-1", "TUB-SUN-100", "material", 30000, "EA", "released", None, None),
        ("SUNB-01", "FAC-1", "SUN-BASE-50", "material", 2500, "KG", "released", "2027-05-31", None),
        ("LBL-01", "FAC-1", "LBL-GEN", "material", 200000, "EA", "released", None, None),
        ("JAR-01", "FAC-1", "JAR-CRM-50", "material", 18000, "EA", "released", None, None),
        ("CRMB-01", "FAC-1", "CRM-BASE-HY", "material", 900, "KG", "released", "2027-02-28", None),
        # scenario 2 + 3: sunscreen
        ("S-B-01", "WH-B", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 1200, "EA", "released", "2027-09-30", None),
        ("S-A-01", "WH-A", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 3600, "EA", "released", "2027-08-31", None),
        ("S-C-01", "WH-C", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 3000, "EA", "released", "2027-06-30", None),
        ("S-C-02", "WH-C", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 1500, "EA", "released", "2026-11-10", None),   # near expiry (20 days)
        ("S-C-03", "WH-C", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 800, "EA", "released", "2026-10-15", None),    # expired
        ("S-C-04", "WH-C", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 700, "EA", "blocked", "2027-07-31", None),     # QA blocked
        ("S-C-05", "WH-C", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 1000, "EA", "reserved", "2027-07-31", "SO-88001"),  # allocated to a customer order
        ("S-C-06", "WH-C", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 500, "EA", "quality_inspection", "2027-08-31", None),  # not released
        # serum finished goods
        ("V-A-01", "WH-A", "SER-VITC-30", "product", 5200, "EA", "released", "2027-12-31", None),
        ("V-B-01", "WH-B", "SER-VITC-30", "product", 2100, "EA", "released", "2027-12-31", None),
        ("V-C-01", "WH-C", "SER-VITC-30", "product", 4100, "EA", "released", "2027-11-30", None),
    ]
    for sku, *_ in PRODUCTS:  # every other SKU gets one released batch per warehouse
        # `sku, *_` takes the first element and ignores the rest of the tuple.
        if sku in ("SUN-SPF50-100", "SER-VITC-30"):
            continue
        for wh in ("WH-A", "WH-B", "WH-C"):
            # Seeded random quantity 800..6000 and expiry 120..700 days ahead.
            inv.append((f"{sku}-{wh}", wh, sku, "product", rng.randint(800, 6000), "EA", "released", _d(rng.randint(120, 700)), None))
    upsert("inventory_batches", ("tenant_id", "batch_id", "location", "item_id", "item_type", "quantity", "uom", "status", "expiry_date", "reserved_for", "snapshot_id"),
           [(t, *row, SNAPSHOT_ID) for row in inv] + [(OTHER_TENANT, "NW-1", "WH-X", "SUN-SPF50-100", "product", 9000, "EA", "released", "2027-12-31", None, "SAP-SYN-NW-2026-10-01")])

    upsert("production_orders", ("tenant_id", "order_id", "sku", "quantity", "uom", "plant", "start_date", "due_date", "status"), [
        (t, "PRD-1001", "SER-VITC-30", 50000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-10-27", "2026-10-30", "released"),
        (t, "PRD-1002", "SUN-SPF50-100", 12000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-11-09", "2026-11-11", "planned"),
        (t, "PRD-1003", "CRM-HYDR-50", 8000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-11-02", "2026-11-04", "planned"),
        (t, "PRD-1004", "SER-RETI-30", 6000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-11-16", "2026-11-18", "planned"),
    ])
    # Flatten SUPPLIERS into supplier rows and supplier_item rows.
    sup_rows, item_rows = [], []
    for sid, name, country, approved, items in SUPPLIERS:
        sup_rows.append((t, sid, name, country, approved))
        item_rows += [(t, sid, m, price, moq, lead) for m, price, moq, lead in items]
    upsert("suppliers", ("tenant_id", "supplier_id", "name", "country", "approved"), sup_rows)
    upsert("supplier_items", ("tenant_id", "supplier_id", "material_id", "unit_price_eur", "moq", "contract_lead_time_days"), item_rows)

    # ---- purchase orders: open/confirmed + ~60 historical receipts (lead-time history for estimation and ML)
    pos = [
        (t, "PO-4500021001", "SUP-A", "PUMP-DISP-24", 25000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-10-15", "2026-11-05", "confirmed", None, None),  # too late for PRD-1001
        (t, "PO-4500021002", "SUP-A", "PUMP-DISP-24", 8000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-10-19", "2026-10-24", "open", None, None),       # not confirmed
        (t, "PO-4500021003", "SUP-C", "BTL-GLS-30", 30000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-10-10", "2026-10-29", "confirmed", None, None),
        (t, "PO-4500021004", "SUP-F", "TUB-SUN-100", 20000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-10-12", "2026-10-28", "confirmed", None, None),
        # the decision used by the outcome-learning scenario: ordered 2026-09-30, promised 5 days, received 9 days later
        (t, "PO-4500020950", "SUP-A", "PUMP-DISP-24", 25000, "EA", "FAC-1", "2026-09-30", "2026-10-05", "received", "2026-10-09", 25000),
    ]
    # True average lead times used to generate the receipt history (SUP-A is slower than its 5-day contract).
    actual_mean = {"SUP-A": 8.6, "SUP-B": 7.4, "SUP-C": 14.5, "SUP-D": 10.8, "SUP-E": 8.3, "SUP-F": 9.6}
    n = 0
    for sid, _, _, approved, items in SUPPLIERS:
        if not approved:
            continue
        for material, _, moq, lead in items:
            # 4 receipts per item for SUP-A/SUP-B (enough for "demonstrated" lead time), 2 for the others.
            for k in range(4 if sid in ("SUP-A", "SUP-B") else 2):
                n += 1
                order = BUSINESS_DATE - timedelta(days=200 - n * 3)
                qty = moq * rng.choice([2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
                # Actual lead = mean +/- 1.6 days noise (+ a small quantity effect for SUP-A, so the ML model has a signal).
                actual = max(1, round(actual_mean[sid] + rng.uniform(-1.6, 1.6) + (0.00004 * qty if sid == "SUP-A" else 0)))
                promised = order + timedelta(days=lead)
                received = order + timedelta(days=actual)
                # Receipts in the future of the snapshot cannot exist yet.
                if received >= BUSINESS_DATE:
                    continue
                short = 0.97 if (sid == "SUP-E" and k == 1) else 1.0  # one partial delivery (incomplete outcome)
                pos.append((t, f"PO-45000{19000 + n}", sid, material, qty, "EA" if material not in ("SER-BASE-VC", "SUN-BASE-50", "CRM-BASE-HY") else "KG",
                            "FAC-1", order.isoformat(), promised.isoformat(), "received", received.isoformat(), round(qty * short)))
    upsert("purchase_orders", ("tenant_id", "po_id", "supplier_id", "material_id", "quantity", "uom", "plant", "order_date", "promised_date",
                               "status", "received_date", "received_quantity"), pos)

    # ---- 90 days of daily sales history per SKU and warehouse (sunscreen + serum follow DEMAND; others random but stable)
    sales = []
    for sku, *_ in PRODUCTS:
        for wh in ("WH-A", "WH-B", "WH-C"):
            # .get(sku, {}).get(wh): planted demand, else a seeded random base 20..160 per day.
            base = DEMAND.get(sku, {}).get(wh) or rng.randint(20, 160)
            for day in range(1, 91):
                weekday = (BUSINESS_DATE - timedelta(days=day)).weekday()
                # Weekly seasonality: Friday (4) and Saturday (5) sell 8% more, other days 3% less.
                season = 1.08 if weekday in (4, 5) else 0.97
                sales.append((t, sku, wh, _d(-day), round(base * season * rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1))))
    upsert("sales_history", ("tenant_id", "sku", "warehouse", "day", "quantity"), sales)
    upsert("transport_lanes", ("tenant_id", "lane_id", "origin", "destination", "mode", "lead_days", "cost_per_unit_eur", "fixed_cost_eur", "capacity_units"),
           [(t, f"LN-{o}-{d}", o, d, mode, lead, cost, fixed, cap) for o, d, mode, lead, cost, fixed, cap in LANES])

    # ---- one prior decision with a verified execution, for the Decision Outcome Learning scenario
    calc = {"kind": "lead_time_estimate", "supplier_id": "SUP-A", "material_id": "PUMP-DISP-24", "predicted_lead_time_days": 5,
            "basis": "contract lead time (baseline v0)", "po_id": "PO-4500020950"}
    upsert("agent_runs", ("id", "tenant_id", "user_id", "kind", "request", "result", "snapshot_id", "created_at"),
           [("CALC-HIST-0001", t, "u-flowise-agent", "lead_time_estimate", json.dumps({"supplier_id": "SUP-A"}), json.dumps(calc), "SAP-SYN-2026-09-30", "2026-09-30T08:00:00+00:00")])
    upsert("recommendations", ("id", "tenant_id", "calculation_id", "domain", "title", "proposed_actions", "evidence", "prediction", "risk_level",
                               "status", "idempotency_key", "model_version", "created_by", "created_at", "updated_at"),
           [("REC-HIST-0001", t, "CALC-HIST-0001", "procurement", "Order 25,000 pumps from Supplier A (predicted 5-day lead time)",
             json.dumps([{"action": "purchase_request", "supplier_id": "SUP-A", "material_id": "PUMP-DISP-24", "quantity": 25000}]),
             json.dumps({"source": "synthetic SAP purchasing history", "snapshot": "SAP-SYN-2026-09-30"}),
             json.dumps({"metric": "lead_time_days", "predicted": 5, "po_id": "PO-4500020950"}), "medium", "executed", "hist-0001", "lead-time-baseline-v0",
             "u-flowise-agent", "2026-09-30T08:00:00+00:00", "2026-09-30T09:30:00+00:00")])
    upsert("human_decisions", ("id", "tenant_id", "recommendation_id", "reviewer_id", "reviewer_roles", "decision", "explanation", "modifications", "created_at"),
           [("HD-HIST-0001", t, "REC-HIST-0001", "u-procurement-manager", json.dumps(["procurement_manager"]), "approve",
             "Supplier A is the qualified primary source; approved.", None, "2026-09-30T09:00:00+00:00")])
    upsert("sap_execution_refs", ("id", "tenant_id", "recommendation_id", "sap_document", "doc_type", "executed_at", "recorded_by", "source"),
           [("SX-HIST-0001", t, "REC-HIST-0001", "PO-4500020950", "purchase_order", "2026-09-30T09:30:00+00:00", "u-sap-executor", "manual_sap_execution_record")])
    # Dict comprehension of row counts for the main tenant (table names are fixed literals).
    return {table: db.one(f"select count(*) as n from {table} where tenant_id=?", (t,))["n"]  # noqa: S608
            for table in ("products", "materials", "inventory_batches", "purchase_orders", "sales_history", "transport_lanes", "suppliers")}

# ===== FUNCTION: load.upsert() =====
    # ID: F0433 · nested · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/fixtures.py:113-119
    # ROLE: Insert rows, ignoring those whose primary key already exists (dialect-specific "insert or ignore").
    # INPUTS:
    #   table: str, cols: tuple of column names, rows: list of value tuples.
    # OUTPUT:
    #   None.
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0432 load() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0424 Database.executemany() (calls)
    def upsert(table: str, cols: tuple, rows: list[tuple]) -> None:
        # "?,?,?" with one "?" per column ("?" * 3 = "???", joined with commas).
        placeholders = ",".join("?" * len(cols))
        if db.dialect == "postgres":
            sql = f"insert into {table}({','.join(cols)}) values({placeholders}) on conflict do nothing"  # noqa: S608
        else:
            sql = f"insert or ignore into {table}({','.join(cols)}) values({placeholders})"  # noqa: S608
        db.executemany(sql, rows)

def build(industry: str, customer: str, spec: dict) -> dict:
    rng = random.Random(f"{industry}/{customer}")
    prefix = spec["prefix"]
    cc = {"FR": "+33", "DE": "+49", "PL": "+48", "US": "+1", "CN": "+86", "NL": "+31", "IE": "+353", "CZ": "+420", "ES": "+34", "IT": "+39", "CH": "+41",
          "SG": "+65", "SE": "+46", "MX": "+52", "HU": "+36", "SK": "+421", "TR": "+90", "GB": "+44"}
    plants = []
    for code, name, ptype, country, city, lat, lon in spec["plants"]:
        roles = ["Warehouse manager", "Inventory control lead", "Transport coordinator"] if ptype == "warehouse" else ["Plant manager", "Production planning lead", "Quality lead"]
        plants.append({"code": code, "name": name, "type": ptype, "country": country, "lat": lat, "lon": lon, "city": city, "zone": ZONE[country],
                       "address": f"{city}, {country} (demo address)", "timezone": "local", "operating_hours": "Mon–Fri 06:00–22:00" if ptype != "warehouse" else "Mon–Sat 06:00–22:00",
                       "contacts": [person(rng, spec["domain"], r, cc.get(country, "+00"), i, i == 0) for i, r in enumerate(roles)],
                       "contacts_note": "Fictional demo contacts (reserved .example domain)."})
    dcs = [p["code"] for p in plants if p["type"] == "warehouse"]
    materials = [{"code": c, "description": d, "type": "FG", "uom": u, "unit_cost": cost, "safety_stock": safety} for c, d, u, cost, safety, *_ in spec["fgs"]]
    materials += [{"code": c, "description": d, "type": t, "uom": u, "unit_cost": cost, "safety_stock": safety} for c, d, t, u, cost, safety in spec["components"]]
    comp = {m["code"]: m for m in materials}
    bom, demand, stock, production, sales, shipments = [], {}, [], [], [], []
    expiry_range = spec.get("expiry_days")
    exp = (lambda: iso(rng.randint(*expiry_range))) if expiry_range else (lambda: None)
    for n, (fg, _desc, _uom, _cost, _safety, dem, cover, plant, lines) in enumerate(spec["fgs"]):
        demand[fg] = dem
        for component, qty, scrap in lines:
            bom.append({"plant": plant, "parent": fg, "component": component, "quantity": qty, "scrap_pct": scrap})
        for dc in dcs:
            # Keep the demo readable: only the first product carries the low-cover hotspots from the spec.
            days = cover[dc] if n == 0 else max(cover[dc], 24)
            stock.append({"plant": dc, "material": fg, "batch": f"{fg[3:9]}-{dc}", "quantity": round(dem[dc] * days), "status": "unrestricted", "expiry": exp()})
        run = round(sum(dem.values()) * rng.choice([10, 12, 14, 18]), -1)
        production.append({"order": f"1{prefix}{n:02d}01", "plant": plant, "material": fg, "quantity": run, "finish_date": iso(rng.randint(6, 12)), "status": "released"})
        production.append({"order": f"1{prefix}{n:02d}02", "plant": plant, "material": fg, "quantity": round(run * 1.3, -1), "finish_date": iso(rng.randint(15, 24)), "status": "planned"})
    # component stock at the producing plants: some short on purpose
    for line in bom:
        need = sum(o["quantity"] for o in production if o["material"] == line["parent"] and o["status"] == "released") * line["quantity"]
        if any(s["plant"] == line["plant"] and s["material"] == line["component"] for s in stock):
            continue
        factor = rng.choice([0.45, 0.7, 1.1, 1.4, 1.8])
        unit = comp[line["component"]]["uom"]
        qty = round(need * factor) if unit == "EA" else round(need * factor, 3)
        stock.append({"plant": line["plant"], "material": line["component"], "batch": f"{line['component'][3:9]}-A", "quantity": qty, "status": "unrestricted", "expiry": exp()})
    # suppliers, POs, receipt history
    suppliers, pos, history, lots = [], [], [], []
    profile_delay = {"good": [0, 0, 1], "avg": [0, 3, 6], "poor": [5, 11, 16]}
    for i, (name, country, city, lat, lon, site, mats, lead, otif, secondary, price, freight, oq, profile) in enumerate(spec["suppliers"]):
        code = f"V-{prefix}{i + 1:03d}"
        suppliers.append({"code": code, "name": name, "country": country, "materials": mats, "contract_lead_time_days": lead, "otif_target_pct": otif, "approved": True,
                          "secondary_source": secondary, "unit_price_eur": price, "freight_eur_per_order": freight, "typical_order_qty": oq, "lat": lat, "lon": lon, "city": city,
                          "manufacturing_country": country, "manufacturing_site": site, "zone": ZONE[country]})
        for m in mats:
            plant = next((b["plant"] for b in bom if b["component"] == m), plants[0]["code"])
            need = sum(o["quantity"] for o in production if o["plant"] == plant) * next(b["quantity"] for b in bom if b["component"] == m)
            unit = comp[m]["uom"]
            qty1 = round(need * 0.35) if unit == "EA" else round(need * 0.35, 3)
            pos.append({"po": f"45{prefix}{len(pos) + 1:05d}", "supplier": name, "material": m, "plant": plant, "quantity": qty1, "delivery_date": iso(rng.randint(3, 9)), "status": "confirmed"})
            pos.append({"po": f"45{prefix}{len(pos) + 1:05d}", "supplier": name, "material": m, "plant": plant, "quantity": qty1, "delivery_date": iso(rng.randint(16, 30)),
                        "status": "confirmed" if rng.random() > 0.25 else "unconfirmed"})
            for k, delay in enumerate(profile_delay[profile]):
                ordered = qty1 or 1
                rejected = round(ordered * (0.08 if profile == "poor" and k == 1 else 0), 3)
                promised = iso(-150 + 50 * k)
                history.append({"po": f"44{prefix}{len(history) + 1:05d}", "supplier": name, "material": m, "promised_date": promised,
                                "received_date": (date.fromisoformat(promised) + timedelta(days=delay)).isoformat(), "quantity_ordered": ordered,
                                "quantity_received": ordered, "quality_rejected": rejected})
        if profile == "poor":
            m = mats[0]
            plant = next((b["plant"] for b in bom if b["component"] == m), plants[0]["code"])
            q = round(max(1, next(s["quantity"] for s in stock if s["material"] == m) * 0.3), 3)
            lots.append({"lot": f"QL-{prefix}{len(lots) + 1:04d}", "plant": plant, "material": m, "batch": f"{m[3:9]}-Q", "quantity": q, "supplier": name, "status": "blocked",
                         "usage_decision": "rejected", "expected_release": None, "defect": "Out-of-specification on incoming inspection"})
            stock.append({"plant": plant, "material": m, "batch": f"{m[3:9]}-Q", "quantity": q, "status": "blocked", "expiry": exp()})
    m = spec["components"][0][0]
    plant = next(b["plant"] for b in bom if b["component"] == m)
    q = round(max(1, next(s["quantity"] for s in stock if s["material"] == m) * 0.15), 3)
    lots.append({"lot": f"QL-{prefix}{len(lots) + 1:04d}", "plant": plant, "material": m, "batch": f"{m[3:9]}-QI", "quantity": q, "supplier": spec["suppliers"][0][0],
                 "status": "inspection", "usage_decision": None, "expected_release": iso(3), "defect": None})
    stock.append({"plant": plant, "material": m, "batch": f"{m[3:9]}-QI", "quantity": q, "status": "quality_inspection", "expiry": exp()})
    # sales orders: one per customer, sized against DC stock so a few are at risk
    fgs = [f[0] for f in spec["fgs"]]
    for i, cust in enumerate(spec["customers"]):
        fg, dc = fgs[i % len(fgs)], dcs[i % len(dcs)]
        on_hand = next(s["quantity"] for s in stock if s["plant"] == dc and s["material"] == fg)
        qty = round(on_hand * (1.25 if i == 0 else rng.choice([0.15, 0.25, 0.35])), -1)  # one order deliberately short
        sales.append({"order": f"SO-{prefix}{7700 + i}", "customer": cust, "warehouse": dc, "material": fg, "quantity": qty, "requested_date": iso(rng.randint(5, 14)),
                      "priority": "high" if i % 3 == 0 else "standard"})
    # lanes between every DC pair (cost/lead by zone)
    lanes = []
    zone_of = {p["code"]: p["zone"] for p in plants}
    for a in dcs:
        for b in dcs:
            if a != b:
                same = zone_of[a] == zone_of[b]
                lanes.append({"from": a, "to": b, "lead_days": rng.choice([2, 3]) if same else rng.choice([9, 14, 21]),
                              "cost_per_unit": round((0.4 if same else 1.6) * (1 + rng.random() / 3), 2), "carbon_kg_per_unit": round((0.06 if same else 0.4) * (1 + rng.random() / 3), 3)})
    carriers = ["DHL Freight", "Maersk", "DB Schenker", "Kuehne+Nagel", "DSV Road", "CMA CGM"]
    shipments.append({"shipment": f"SH-{prefix}01", "type": "stock_transfer", "from": dcs[0], "to": dcs[1], "material": fgs[0], "quantity": round(demand[fgs[0]][dcs[1]] * 3, -1),
                      "carrier": carriers[0], "mode": "road", "departed": iso(-3), "eta": iso(1), "status": "in_transit", "delay_days": 2, "delay_reason": "Border congestion"})
    shipments.append({"shipment": f"SH-{prefix}02", "type": "stock_transfer", "from": dcs[0], "to": dcs[-1], "material": fgs[1], "quantity": round(demand[fgs[1]][dcs[-1]] * 4, -1),
                      "carrier": carriers[1], "mode": "sea", "departed": iso(-12), "eta": iso(4), "status": "in_transit", "delay_days": 6, "delay_reason": "Port congestion"})
    first_sup = suppliers[0]
    shipments.append({"shipment": f"SH-{prefix}03", "type": "inbound", "from": first_sup["code"], "to": next(b["plant"] for b in bom if b["component"] in first_sup["materials"]),
                      "material": first_sup["materials"][0], "quantity": pos[0]["quantity"], "carrier": carriers[2], "mode": "road", "departed": iso(-1), "eta": pos[0]["delivery_date"],
                      "status": "in_transit", "delay_days": 0, "delay_reason": None})
    # stocktake counts + goods movements (one explained, one within tolerance, one to investigate, one matched)
    fg_rows = [s for s in stock if s["material"] in fgs and s["plant"] in dcs]
    a, b, c, d = fg_rows[0], fg_rows[1], fg_rows[2], fg_rows[3]
    counts = [
        {"count_id": f"PI-{prefix}-01", "count_date": iso(-1), "plant": a["plant"], "material": a["material"], "batch": a["batch"], "book_quantity": a["quantity"], "counted_quantity": a["quantity"] - 40, "counter": "Night shift"},
        {"count_id": f"PI-{prefix}-02", "count_date": iso(-1), "plant": b["plant"], "material": b["material"], "batch": b["batch"], "book_quantity": b["quantity"], "counted_quantity": b["quantity"] - max(1, round(b["quantity"] * 0.004)), "counter": "Cycle count A"},
        {"count_id": f"PI-{prefix}-03", "count_date": iso(-1), "plant": c["plant"], "material": c["material"], "batch": c["batch"], "book_quantity": c["quantity"], "counted_quantity": round(c["quantity"] * 0.96), "counter": "Cycle count B"},
        {"count_id": f"PI-{prefix}-04", "count_date": iso(-1), "plant": d["plant"], "material": d["material"], "batch": d["batch"], "book_quantity": d["quantity"], "counted_quantity": d["quantity"], "counter": "Cycle count C"},
    ]
    movements = [{"document": f"49{prefix}0001", "type": "goods_issue", "plant": a["plant"], "material": a["material"], "batch": a["batch"], "quantity": -40, "date": iso(-2),
                  "posted": False, "reference": "Samples issued, posting pending"}]
    snapshot = {"id": f"SAP-{prefix}-2026-10-20T040000Z", "source_system": f"S4HANA-{industry.upper()}-DEMO", "extracted_at": "2026-10-20T04:00:00+00:00",
                "as_of_date": AS_OF.isoformat(), "read_only": True, "modules": ["MM", "PP", "QM", "SD", "PUR", "WM", "LE"],
                "industry": industry, "customer": spec["company"], "synthetic": True}
    quotes = [{"supplier": s, "material": m, "unit_price_eur": p, "freight_eur_per_order": f, "typical_order_qty": q, "quoted_lead_time_days": lt, "qualified": ok,
               "country": c2, "city": city, "lat": lat, "lon": lon, "zone": ZONE[c2], "reference": "approved secondary source" if ok else "qualification in progress"}
              for s, m, p, f, q, lt, ok, c2, city, lat, lon in spec["quotes"]]
    origins = [{"ingredient": ing, "origin": o, "country": c2, "lat": lat, "lon": lon, "feeds_supplier": fs, "feeds_material": fm, "share_of_material_pct": sh, "transit_days": t,
                "transit_variability_days": v, "criticality": crit, "alternatives": "see sourcing plan", "note": note}
               for ing, o, c2, lat, lon, fs, fm, sh, t, v, crit, note in spec["origins"]]
    return {"snapshot": snapshot, "plants": plants, "materials": materials, "suppliers": suppliers, "bom": bom, "stock": stock, "purchase_orders": pos,
            "po_history": history, "production_orders": production, "quality_lots": lots, "sales_orders": sales, "shipments": shipments,
            "stocktake_counts": counts, "goods_movements": movements, "warehouse_demand_daily": demand, "lanes": lanes, "supplier_quotes": quotes,
            "ingredient_origins": origins}

def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    index = {"default": "cosmetics/aurelia", "industries": {k: {"label": v, "customers": []} for k, v in INDUSTRIES.items()}}
    index["industries"]["cosmetics"]["customers"].append({"id": "aurelia", "name": "Aurelia Cosmetics", "file": "data/sap_mock.json", "synthetic": True})
    for (industry, customer), spec in SPECS.items():
        data = build(industry, customer, spec)
        file = OUT / f"{industry}__{customer}.json"
        file.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        index["industries"][industry]["customers"].append({"id": customer, "name": spec["company"], "file": f"data/tenants/{file.name}", "synthetic": True})
        print(f"{industry:15} {spec['company']:28} {len(data['materials'])} materials, {len(data['suppliers'])} suppliers, {len(data['plants'])} sites")
    (OUT / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

# ===== FUNCTION: LocalBackend._save() =====
    # ID: F0453 · method · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/copilot.py:46-48
    # ROLE: Store an analysis and return it in the gateway's response shape (analysis_id + snapshot + read_only + result).
    # INPUTS:
    #   kind: str, request: dict, result: dict.
    # OUTPUT:
    #   dict.
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0455 LocalBackend.factory_readiness() (calls)
    #   <- F0456 LocalBackend.stock_balance() (calls)
    #   <- F0457 LocalBackend.demand_forecast() (calls)
    #   <- F0458 LocalBackend.supplier_risk() (calls)
    #   <- F0459 LocalBackend.quality_status() (calls)
    #   <- F0460 LocalBackend.logistics_status() (calls)
    #   <- F0462 LocalBackend.sales_orders() (calls)
    #   <- F0463 LocalBackend.stocktake() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0361 Store.save_analysis() (calls)
    #   -> F0405 SapRepository.snapshot() (references)
    def _save(self, kind: str, request: dict, result: dict) -> dict:
        analysis_id = self.store.save_analysis(kind, request, result, self.sap.snapshot["id"], self.actor)
        return {"analysis_id": analysis_id, "snapshot": self.sap.snapshot, "read_only": True, **result}

# ===== FUNCTION: LocalBackend.factory_readiness() =====
    # ID: F0455 · method · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/copilot.py:58-60
    # ROLE: Engine factory readiness (need_by given as an ISO string by the agent), stored.
    # INPUTS:
    #   plant, material: str; quantity: float; need_by: str.
    # OUTPUT:
    #   dict.
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0592 run_factory() (calls)
    #   <- F0487 factory_material_readiness() (references)
    #   <- F0504 factory_material_readiness() (references)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0453 LocalBackend._save() (calls)
    #   -> F0197 SupplyChainEngine.factory_readiness() (calls)

# ===== FUNCTION: ApiBackend._call() =====
    # ID: F0469 · method · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/copilot.py:105-113
    # ROLE: Send a request; >= 400 raises ApiError with the gateway's detail; else return the JSON body.
    # INPUTS:
    #   method: str, path: str, **kwargs (json=..., params=...).
    # OUTPUT:
    #   dict.
    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0471 ApiBackend.snapshot() (calls)
    #   <- F0472 ApiBackend.factory_readiness() (calls)
    #   <- F0473 ApiBackend.stock_balance() (calls)
    #   <- F0474 ApiBackend.demand_forecast() (calls)
    #   <- F0475 ApiBackend.supplier_risk() (calls)
    #   <- F0476 ApiBackend.quality_status() (calls)
    #   <- F0477 ApiBackend.logistics_status() (calls)
    #   <- F0478 ApiBackend.inventory() (calls)
    #   <- F0479 ApiBackend.sales_orders() (calls)
    #   <- F0480 ApiBackend.stocktake() (calls)
    #   <- F0481 ApiBackend.search_knowledge() (calls)
    #   <- F0482 ApiBackend.submit_recommendation() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   -> F0466 ApiError (calls)
    def _call(self, method: str, path: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
        response = self._client.request(method, path, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code >= 400:
            try:
                detail = response.json()
            except ValueError:
                detail = response.text
            raise ApiError(f"{method} {path} -> {response.status_code}: {detail}")
        return response.json()

# ===== FUNCTION: ApiBackend._clean() =====
    # ID: F0470 · method · used
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/copilot.py:115-117
    # ROLE: Drop None / empty values so the strict gateway schemas do not receive empty optional fields.
    # INPUTS:

    # OUTPUT:

    # CALLED BY:
    #   <- F0474 ApiBackend.demand_forecast() (calls)

    #   <- F0481 ApiBackend.search_knowledge() (calls)
    # CALLS:
    #   (none found)
    @staticmethod
    def _clean(payload: dict) -> dict:
        return {key: value for key, value in payload.items() if value not in (None, "")}

#   -> F0451 LocalBackend (calls)
#   -> F0438 CopilotBackend (references)
def build_backend(settings: Settings, actor: str = "langgraph") -> CopilotBackend:
    if settings.copilot_api_url:
        return ApiBackend(settings.copilot_api_url, settings.copilot_api_key)
    sap = SapRepository(settings.data_file)
    try:
        rag = create_rag(settings.rag_backend, settings.postgres_url, settings.knowledge_dir, settings.embedding_backend, settings.embedding_model)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - offline fallback keeps graphs loadable for Studio without Postgres
        rag = MemoryRag()
        rag.load_directory(settings.knowledge_dir)
    return LocalBackend(sap, rag, actor=actor)

# ===== FUNCTION: ApiKeyMiddleware.dispatch() =====
    # ID: F0499 · method · used (framework)
    # ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/mcp_server.py:108-114
    # ROLE: Check the key, then pass the request on (await call_next) or answer 401.
    # INPUTS:
    #   request: Request, call_next: async callable.
    # OUTPUT:
    #   Response.
    # CALLED BY:
    #   (none found)
    # CALLS:
    #   (none found)
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        if request.url.path == "/health" or not self.keys:
            return await call_next(request)
        supplied = request.headers.get("x-api-key") or request.headers.get("authorization", "").removeprefix("Bearer ").strip()
        if supplied and any(hmac.compare_digest(supplied.encode(), key) for key in self.keys):
            return await call_next(request)
        return JSONResponse({"error": "missing or invalid MCP API key"}, status_code=401)

# CALLED BY:

def _safe(fn, *args, **kwargs) -> str:

def ask_langgraph(q: str) -> dict:
    t = time.time()
    status, thread = http(f"{LANGGRAPH}/threads", {})
    tid = (thread or {}).get("thread_id") if isinstance(thread, dict) else None
    if not tid:  # e.g. the LangGraph server is restarting: record the failure, keep going
        return {"ok": False, "status": status, "secs": time.time() - t, "text": "", "intent": "", "paused": False, "handle": {}, "error": "no thread"}
    status, v = http(f"{LANGGRAPH}/threads/{tid}/runs/wait", {"assistant_id": "scinsight_supervisor", "input": {"messages": [{"type": "human", "content": q}]}})
    secs = time.time() - t
    _, st = http(f"{LANGGRAPH}/threads/{tid}/state")
    values = (st or {}).get("values") or (v if isinstance(v, dict) else {})
    paused = "human_approval" in ((st or {}).get("next") or [])
    text = values.get("answer") or ""
    return {"ok": status == 200 and "__error__" not in (v or {}), "status": status, "secs": secs, "text": text, "intent": values.get("intent", ""),
            "paused": paused, "handle": {"thread": tid}, "error": (v or {}).get("__error__") if isinstance(v, dict) else None}

def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=5, help="questions per role (1-5)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    data = json.loads((ROOT / "data" / "scinsight" / "role_questions.json").read_text())
    cases = [(r["title"], q) for r in data["roles"] for q in r["questions"][: args.limit]] + [("Guard", g) for g in data["guards"]]
    rows = []
    for i, (role, case) in enumerate(cases, 1):
        expected = case["intent"] if isinstance(case["intent"], list) else [case["intent"]]
        row = {"role": role, "q": case["q"], "expected": " or ".join(expected)}
        for name, ask in (("flowise", ask_flowise), ("langgraph", ask_langgraph)):
            try:
                r = ask(case["q"])
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - one broken call must not stop the comparison
                r = {"ok": False, "status": 0, "secs": 0, "text": "", "intent": "", "paused": False, "error": str(e)[:200]}
            facts, why = check_facts(r["text"], case["expect"]) if r["ok"] else (False, f"HTTP {r['status']} {r.get('error') or ''}")
            row[name] = {"ok": r["ok"], "route_ok": r["intent"] in expected, "intent": r["intent"], "facts_ok": facts, "why": why,
                         "paused": r["paused"], "secs": round(r["secs"], 1)}
        f, lg = row["flowise"], row["langgraph"]
        print(f"[{i:2}/{len(cases)}] {role:22} F:{'route' if f['route_ok'] else 'ROUTE?'}/{'facts' if f['facts_ok'] else 'FACTS?'} {f['secs']:5.1f}s | "
              f"LG:{'route' if lg['route_ok'] else 'ROUTE?'}/{'facts' if lg['facts_ok'] else 'FACTS?'} {lg['secs']:5.1f}s | {case['q'][:60]}", flush=True)
        rows.append(row)
    cycles = {name: approval_cycle(name) for name in ("flowise", "langgraph")}
    print("approval cycle:", json.dumps(cycles))
    stamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    (ROOT / "deploy-evidence").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (ROOT / "deploy-evidence" / f"compare-{stamp}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"rows": rows, "approval": cycles}, indent=1))
    write_report(rows, cycles, stamp)
    return 0

def write_report(rows: list[dict], cycles: dict, stamp: str) -> None:
    def stats(name: str) -> dict:
        rs = [r[name] for r in rows]
        secs = [r["secs"] for r in rs if r["ok"]]
        return {"route": sum(r["route_ok"] for r in rs), "facts": sum(r["facts_ok"] for r in rs), "errors": sum(not r["ok"] for r in rs),
                "paused": sum(r["paused"] for r in rs), "median": statistics.median(secs) if secs else 0, "mean": statistics.mean(secs) if secs else 0, "n": len(rs)}
    s = {n: stats(n) for n in ("flowise", "langgraph")}
    mark = lambda ok: "✓" if ok else "✗"  # noqa: E731
    lines = [
        "# Flowise vs LangGraph: same SCInsight agent, two runtimes", "",
        f"Run {stamp} UTC on this machine (Qwen 2.5 7B via Ollama, temperature 0). Both runtimes call the same SCInsight API with the same agent key "
        "and use the same prompt files, so differences come from the runtime, not the design. Produced by `scripts/scinsight_compare.py`.", "",
        "| | Flowise (Agentflow V2) | LangGraph (StateGraph) |", "|---|---|---|",
        f"| Right specialist chosen | {s['flowise']['route']}/{s['flowise']['n']} | {s['langgraph']['route']}/{s['langgraph']['n']} |",
        f"| Facts correct (checked on the cited calculation) | {s['flowise']['facts']}/{s['flowise']['n']} | {s['langgraph']['facts']}/{s['langgraph']['n']} |",
        f"| Errors | {s['flowise']['errors']} | {s['langgraph']['errors']} |",
        f"| Paused for approval | {s['flowise']['paused']} | {s['langgraph']['paused']} |",
        f"| Median / mean time per question | {s['flowise']['median']:.1f} s / {s['flowise']['mean']:.1f} s | {s['langgraph']['median']:.1f} s / {s['langgraph']['mean']:.1f} s |",
        f"| Approval cycle (pause → manager approves in API → resume → verified) | {mark(cycles['flowise']['ok'])} | {mark(cycles['langgraph']['ok'])} |", "",
        "## Per question", "", "| Role | Question | Expected | Flowise route · facts · time | LangGraph route · facts · time |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in rows:
        cell = lambda x: f"{mark(x['route_ok'])} {x['intent'] or '—'} · {mark(x['facts_ok'])}{' ' + x['why'] if x['why'] else ''} · {x['secs']} s"  # noqa: E731
        lines.append(f"| {r['role']} | {r['q']} | {r['expected']} | {cell(r['flowise'])} | {cell(r['langgraph'])} |")
    (ROOT / "docs" / "scinsight" / "FLOWISE_VS_LANGGRAPH_RESULTS.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(s))

# ===== FUNCTION: _history() =====
# ID: F0524 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/forecasting.py:10-13
# ROLE: Synthetic daily demand history: base level x (1 + slight trend + weekly + monthly seasonality).
# INPUTS:
#   base: float (average units per day), days: int (180).
# OUTPUT:
#   np.ndarray -> one value per day.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0527 backtest() (calls)
#   <- F0529 evaluate_models() (calls)
#   <- F0530 pooled_evaluation() (calls)
#   <- F0531 forecast() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   (none found)
def _history(base: float, days: int = 180) -> np.ndarray:
    # Reproducible synthetic SAP history with weekly seasonality and a mild trend.
    x = np.arange(days, dtype=float)
    return base * (1 + 0.0015 * x + 0.16 * np.sin(2 * math.pi * x / 7) + 0.05 * np.sin(2 * math.pi * x / 30))

# ===== FUNCTION: _features() =====
# ID: F0525 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/forecasting.py:16-25
# ROLE: Feature matrix for day indexes: trend + sin/cos of the weekly and monthly cycles.
# INPUTS:
#   day_indexes: np.ndarray.
# OUTPUT:
#   np.ndarray -> shape (n, 5).
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0526 _fit_predict() (calls)
#   <- F0530 pooled_evaluation() (calls)
#   <- F0531 forecast() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   (none found)
def _features(day_indexes: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    # column_stack: put the 5 one-dimensional arrays side by side as columns.
    return np.column_stack(
        [
            day_indexes,
            np.sin(2 * math.pi * day_indexes / 7),
            np.cos(2 * math.pi * day_indexes / 7),
            np.sin(2 * math.pi * day_indexes / 30),
            np.cos(2 * math.pi * day_indexes / 30),
        ]
    )

# ===== FUNCTION: _fit_predict() =====
# ID: F0526 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/forecasting.py:28-37
# ROLE: Fit on train_days and predict predict_days with XGBoost (fallback: a linear trend if xgboost is not installed).
# INPUTS:
#   history: np.ndarray, train_days: np.ndarray, predict_days: np.ndarray.
# OUTPUT:
#   tuple[np.ndarray, str] -> (predictions, engine name).
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0527 backtest() (calls)
#   <- F0529 evaluate_models() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0525 _features() (calls)
def _fit_predict(history: np.ndarray, train_days: np.ndarray, predict_days: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, str]:
    try:
        from xgboost import XGBRegressor

        # Fixed hyper-parameters and random_state=42, n_jobs=1 -> identical results on every run.
        model = XGBRegressor(n_estimators=100, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.06, subsample=0.9, random_state=42, n_jobs=1)
        # history[train_days.astype(int)]: the target values of the training days (fancy indexing).
        model.fit(_features(train_days), history[train_days.astype(int)])
        return model.predict(_features(predict_days)), "xgboost"
    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
        coefficients = np.polyfit(train_days, history[train_days.astype(int)], 1)
        return np.polyval(coefficients, predict_days), "linear-fallback"

# ===== FUNCTION: backtest() =====
# ID: F0527 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/forecasting.py:40-59
# ROLE: Forecast vs actuals for charts: train without the last `holdout_days`, predict them (back-test, MAPE), then retrain on all
#       days and forecast the future horizon.
# INPUTS:
#   base_daily_demand: float, holdout_days: int (14), horizon_days: int (14), show_days: int (45 days of actuals shown).
# OUTPUT:
#   dict -> engine, offsets_*/actual/backtest/forecast series, holdout_mape_pct, holdout_days.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0209 SupplyChainEngine.forecast_vs_actuals() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0524 _history() (calls)
#   -> F0526 _fit_predict() (calls)
@lru_cache(maxsize=64)
def backtest(base_daily_demand: float, holdout_days: int = 14, horizon_days: int = 14, show_days: int = 45) -> dict:
    """Forecast vs actuals: train without the last `holdout_days`, predict them, then forecast the future horizon."""
    history = _history(base_daily_demand)
    n = history.size
    holdout_pred, engine = _fit_predict(history, np.arange(n - holdout_days, dtype=float), np.arange(n - holdout_days, n, dtype=float))
    future_pred, _ = _fit_predict(history, np.arange(n, dtype=float), np.arange(n, n + horizon_days, dtype=float))
    actual = history[n - holdout_days:]
    # MAPE = mean(|actual - predicted| / actual) x 100 (np.maximum avoids division by zero).
    mape = float(np.mean(np.abs(actual - holdout_pred) / np.maximum(actual, 1e-6)) * 100)
    return {
        "engine": engine,
        "offsets_actual": list(range(-show_days, 0)),
        "actual": [round(float(v), 1) for v in history[n - show_days:]],
        "offsets_backtest": list(range(-holdout_days, 0)),
        "backtest": [round(float(v), 1) for v in holdout_pred],
        "offsets_forecast": list(range(0, horizon_days)),
        "forecast": [round(max(0.0, float(v)), 1) for v in future_pred],
        "holdout_mape_pct": round(mape, 2),
        "holdout_days": holdout_days,
    }

# ===== FUNCTION: _errors() =====
# ID: F0528 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/forecasting.py:62-66
# ROLE: Error metrics: WAPE %, bias %, MAE.
# INPUTS:
#   actual: np.ndarray, predicted: np.ndarray.
# OUTPUT:
#   dict.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0529 evaluate_models() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   (none found)
def _errors(actual: np.ndarray, predicted: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    err = predicted - actual
    total = float(np.sum(actual)) or 1e-6
    return {"wape_pct": round(float(np.sum(np.abs(err)) / total * 100), 2), "bias_pct": round(float(np.sum(err) / total * 100), 2),
            "mae": round(float(np.mean(np.abs(err))), 2)}

# ===== FUNCTION: evaluate_models() =====
# ID: F0529 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/forecasting.py:69-88
# ROLE: Model quality on the same holdout: XGBoost vs seasonal naive (same weekday last week), error reduction, drift
#       (error of the recent half vs the earlier half of the holdout), demand coefficient of variation.
# INPUTS:
#   base_daily_demand: float, holdout_days: int (14).
# OUTPUT:
#   dict -> engine, model, baseline, error_reduction_pct, drift, demand_cv_pct.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0254 MoatEngine.model_comparison() (calls)
#   <- F0261 RoleCenter._facts() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0524 _history() (calls)
#   -> F0526 _fit_predict() (calls)
#   -> F0528 _errors() (calls)
@lru_cache(maxsize=64)
def evaluate_models(base_daily_demand: float, holdout_days: int = 14) -> dict:
    """Model quality on the same holdout: XGBoost vs a seasonal-naive baseline (same weekday last week).
    Drift = error on the most recent 7 days vs the 7 days before (both out of sample)."""
    history = _history(base_daily_demand)
    n = history.size
    days = np.arange(n - holdout_days, n, dtype=float)
    xgb, engine = _fit_predict(history, np.arange(n - holdout_days, dtype=float), days)
    actual = history[n - holdout_days:]
    # Seasonal naive: the values 7 days earlier.
    naive = history[n - holdout_days - 7:n - 7]
    model, baseline = _errors(actual, xgb), _errors(actual, naive)
    half = holdout_days // 2
    earlier, recent = _errors(actual[:half], xgb[:half]), _errors(actual[half:], xgb[half:])
    return {
        "engine": engine, "holdout_days": holdout_days, "model": model, "baseline": {"name": "seasonal naive (same weekday last week)", **baseline},
        "error_reduction_pct": round(100 * (1 - model["wape_pct"] / baseline["wape_pct"]), 1) if baseline["wape_pct"] else None,
        "drift": {"earlier_wape_pct": earlier["wape_pct"], "recent_wape_pct": recent["wape_pct"],
                  "change_pts": round(recent["wape_pct"] - earlier["wape_pct"], 2)},
        "demand_cv_pct": round(float(np.std(history[-28:]) / np.mean(history[-28:]) * 100), 1),
    }

# ===== FUNCTION: pooled_evaluation() =====
# ID: F0530 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/forecasting.py:91-126
# ROLE: Pooled ("industry") model: train one XGBoost on demand-normalised series of several customers and score it on the target
#       customer's holdout; options to exclude the target's history and to simulate a cold start (scale by planned demand only).
# INPUTS:
#   target_bases: tuple[float, ...], donor_bases: tuple[float, ...], include_target: bool, scale_by_history: bool (True), holdout_days: int (14).
#   (tuples, not lists, because lru_cache needs hashable arguments)
# OUTPUT:
#   dict | None -> {"wape_pct", "series", "training_series"}, or None without training data.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0254 MoatEngine.model_comparison() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0524 _history() (calls)
#   -> F0525 _features() (calls)
@lru_cache(maxsize=256)
def pooled_evaluation(target_bases: tuple[float, ...], donor_bases: tuple[float, ...], include_target: bool,
                      scale_by_history: bool = True, holdout_days: int = 14) -> dict | None:
    """Train one model on demand-normalised series from several customers and score it on the target customer's holdout.

    include_target=False: the target's history is not used for training. scale_by_history=False is a cold start: the
    forecast is scaled by the planned daily demand level only (what a newly onboarded customer has on day one).
    Returns None without training data."""
    n = _history(1.0).size
    xs, ys = [], []
    for base in donor_bases:  # other (consenting) customers: their full history
        history = _history(base)
        xs.append(_features(np.arange(n, dtype=float)))
        # Normalise by the series' own mean so different volume levels can be pooled.
        ys.append(history / history[:n - holdout_days].mean())
    if include_target:
        for base in target_bases:  # the target's own history, never its holdout
            history = _history(base)
            days = np.arange(n - holdout_days, dtype=float)
            xs.append(_features(days))
            ys.append(history[: n - holdout_days] / history[: n - holdout_days].mean())
    if not xs or not target_bases:
        return None
    from xgboost import XGBRegressor

    model = XGBRegressor(n_estimators=100, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.06, subsample=0.9, random_state=42, n_jobs=1)
    # vstack / concatenate: stack all series' rows into one training set.
    model.fit(np.vstack(xs), np.concatenate(ys))
    holdout = np.arange(n - holdout_days, n, dtype=float)
    abs_err = total = 0.0
    for base in target_bases:
        history = _history(base)
        # Scale the normalised prediction back to units: history mean (normal) or planned level (cold start).
        scale = history[: n - holdout_days].mean() if scale_by_history else base
        predicted = model.predict(_features(holdout)) * scale
        actual = history[n - holdout_days:]
        abs_err += float(np.sum(np.abs(predicted - actual)))
        total += float(np.sum(actual))
    return {"wape_pct": round(100 * abs_err / total, 2), "series": len(target_bases), "training_series": len(donor_bases) + (len(target_bases) if include_target else 0)}

# ===== FUNCTION: forecast() =====
# ID: F0531 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/forecasting.py:129-157
# ROLE: The forecast used by the engine: train on the full history and forecast `horizon_days` daily values (never negative),
#       with the in-sample training MAE.
# INPUTS:
#   base_daily_demand: float, horizon_days: int.
# OUTPUT:
#   dict -> engine, horizon_days, daily_forecast[], total_forecast, training_rows, training_mae, model_scope.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0198 SupplyChainEngine.stock_balance() (calls)
#   <- F0199 SupplyChainEngine.demand_forecast() (calls)
#   <- F0212 SupplyChainEngine.product_360() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0524 _history() (calls)
#   -> F0525 _features() (calls)
@lru_cache(maxsize=64)
def forecast(base_daily_demand: float, horizon_days: int) -> dict:
    history = _history(base_daily_demand)
    train_days = np.arange(history.size, dtype=float)
    future_days = np.arange(history.size, history.size + horizon_days, dtype=float)
    engine = "xgboost"
    try:
        from xgboost import XGBRegressor

        model = XGBRegressor(n_estimators=100, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.06, subsample=0.9, random_state=42, n_jobs=1)
        model.fit(_features(train_days), history)
        predicted = model.predict(_features(future_days))
        fitted = model.predict(_features(train_days))
    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - minimal emergency install only
        engine = "linear-fallback"
        coefficients = np.polyfit(train_days, history, 1)
        predicted = np.polyval(coefficients, future_days)
        fitted = np.polyval(coefficients, train_days)
    mae = float(np.mean(np.abs(history - fitted)))
    values = [round(max(0.0, float(value)), 2) for value in predicted]
    return {
        "engine": engine,
        "horizon_days": horizon_days,
        "daily_forecast": values,
        "total_forecast": round(sum(values), 2),
        "training_rows": int(history.size),
        "training_mae": round(mae, 3),
        "model_scope": "synthetic POC history; replace with approved SAP billing history before production",
    }

# ===== FUNCTION: _rows() =====
# ID: F0532 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/learning.py:24-35
# ROLE: Training rows = received POs joined with their contract lead time, ordered by order date, deduplicated, with the
#       actual lead time in days added as "lead".
# INPUTS:
#   db: Database, tenant: str.
# OUTPUT:
#   list[dict] -> purchase_orders rows + contract_lead_time_days + lead.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0534 train_lead_time_model() (calls)
#   <- F0536 predict_lead_time() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0418 Database (references)
#   -> F0421 Database.query() (calls)
def _rows(db: Database, tenant: str) -> list[dict]:
    rows = db.query("select po.*, si.contract_lead_time_days from purchase_orders po join supplier_items si on si.tenant_id=po.tenant_id "
                    "and si.supplier_id=po.supplier_id and si.material_id=po.material_id where po.tenant_id=? and po.received_date is not null "
                    "order by po.order_date, po.po_id", (tenant,))
    seen, out = set(), []
    for r in rows:  # duplicate receipts are counted once
        if r["po_id"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(r["po_id"])
        # Label: receipt date - order date, in days.
        r["lead"] = (date.fromisoformat(r["received_date"]) - date.fromisoformat(r["order_date"])).days
        out.append(r)
    return out

# ===== FUNCTION: _features() =====
# ID: F0533 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/learning.py:38-40
# ROLE: Feature matrix: supplier one-hot + log(1 + quantity) + order month + contract lead time.
# INPUTS:
#   rows: list[dict], suppliers: list[str] (fixed column order of the one-hot part).
# OUTPUT:
#   np.ndarray -> shape (n_rows, len(suppliers) + 3).
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0534 train_lead_time_model() (calls)
#   <- F0536 predict_lead_time() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   (none found)
def _features(rows: list[dict], suppliers: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
    # List concatenation inside the comprehension builds one feature row per PO.
    return np.array([[1.0 if r["supplier_id"] == s else 0.0 for s in suppliers] + [math.log1p(float(r["quantity"])),
                     float(date.fromisoformat(r["order_date"]).month), float(r["contract_lead_time_days"])] for r in rows])

# ===== FUNCTION: train_lead_time_model() =====
# ID: F0534 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/learning.py:43-70
# ROLE: Train a CANDIDATE lead-time model: time split 75/25, fit gradient boosting, compute MAE/bias on the holdout and the
#       MAE of two baselines (contract lead time, supplier mean); store a model_versions row with status "candidate".
# INPUTS:
#   db: Database, tenant: str, user_id: str (who trained it — kept for the route's audit).
# OUTPUT:
#   dict -> model_version_id, version, status, train_rows, holdout_rows, metrics, baselines, beats_best_baseline, note.
# RAISES:
#   HTTPException 409 when there are fewer than 20 receipts.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0143 create_app.train() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0418 Database (references)
#   -> F0532 _rows() (calls)
#   -> F0533 _features() (calls)
#   -> F0416 now_iso() (calls)
#   -> F0423 Database.execute() (calls)
def train_lead_time_model(db: Database, tenant: str, user_id: str) -> dict:
    rows = _rows(db, tenant)
    if len(rows) < 20:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"only {len(rows)} goods receipts; at least 20 are needed for a meaningful holdout")
    # Rows are sorted by order date -> the latest 25% are the holdout (no future data leaks into training).
    cut = int(len(rows) * 0.75)
    train, hold = rows[:cut], rows[cut:]
    suppliers = sorted({r["supplier_id"] for r in rows})
    # Small, fixed hyper-parameters and random_state=7 -> fully reproducible.
    model = GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=150, max_depth=2, learning_rate=0.05, random_state=7)
    model.fit(_features(train, suppliers), [r["lead"] for r in train])
    actual = np.array([r["lead"] for r in hold], dtype=float)
    pred = model.predict(_features(hold, suppliers))
    # Baseline (b): mean lead per supplier on the TRAINING set (suppliers absent from training fall back to the overall mean).
    sup_mean = {s: float(np.mean([r["lead"] for r in train if r["supplier_id"] == s])) for s in suppliers if any(r["supplier_id"] == s for r in train)}
    overall = float(np.mean([r["lead"] for r in train]))
    base_contract = np.array([float(r["contract_lead_time_days"]) for r in hold])
    base_mean = np.array([sup_mean.get(r["supplier_id"], overall) for r in hold])
    # Mean absolute error helper (lambda assigned to a name).
    mae = lambda p: round(float(np.mean(np.abs(actual - p))), 3)  # noqa: E731
    metrics = {"mae_days": mae(pred), "bias_days": round(float(np.mean(pred - actual)), 3)}
    baselines = {"contract_lead_time_mae_days": mae(base_contract), "supplier_mean_mae_days": mae(base_mean)}
    version = f"lt-gbr-{now_iso()[:10]}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
    mid = f"MV-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:10].upper()}"
    # The algorithm column documents the exact configuration; the suppliers list is kept in metrics for re-fitting.
    db.execute("insert into model_versions(id,tenant_id,model_name,version,algorithm,trained_at,train_rows,holdout_rows,metrics,baseline_metrics,status) "
               "values(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
               (mid, tenant, MODEL_NAME, version, "sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor(n=150, depth=2, lr=0.05, seed=7); features: supplier one-hot, "
                "log(quantity), order month, contract lead time", now_iso(), len(train), len(hold), json.dumps({**metrics, "suppliers": suppliers}), json.dumps(baselines), "candidate"))
    best_baseline = min(baselines.values())
    return {"model_version_id": mid, "version": version, "status": "candidate", "train_rows": len(train), "holdout_rows": len(hold),
            "metrics": metrics, "baselines": baselines, "beats_best_baseline": metrics["mae_days"] < best_baseline,
            "note": "Synthetic history: results demonstrate the governed pipeline, not real supplier performance. Promotion is manual."}

# ===== FUNCTION: promote() =====
# ID: F0535 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/learning.py:73-85
# ROLE: Promotion gate: a candidate is promoted only if its holdout MAE beats the best baseline; otherwise it is rejected.
#       The previously promoted model is superseded in the same transaction.
# INPUTS:
#   db: Database, tenant: str, model_id: str, user_id: str (the director).
# OUTPUT:
#   dict -> promoted model_versions row + {"gate": "passed: ..."}.
# RAISES:
#   HTTPException 404 (unknown), 409 (not a candidate / gate failed).
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0144 create_app.promote() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0418 Database (references)
#   -> F0422 Database.one() (calls)
#   -> F0423 Database.execute() (calls)
#   -> F0425 Database.transaction() (calls)
#   -> F0416 now_iso() (calls)
def promote(db: Database, tenant: str, model_id: str, user_id: str) -> dict:
    row = db.one("select * from model_versions where id=? and tenant_id=?", (model_id, tenant))
    if row is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="model version not found")
    if row["status"] != "candidate":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"model version is {row['status']}")
    metrics, baselines = json.loads(row["metrics"]), json.loads(row["baseline_metrics"])
    if metrics["mae_days"] >= min(baselines.values()):
        # Record the rejection, then refuse.
        db.execute("update model_versions set status='rejected' where id=?", (model_id,))
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"promotion gate: model MAE {metrics['mae_days']} does not beat the best baseline {min(baselines.values())}; rejected")
    db.transaction([("update model_versions set status='superseded' where tenant_id=? and model_name=? and status='promoted'", (tenant, row["model_name"])),
                    ("update model_versions set status='promoted', promoted_by=?, promoted_at=? where id=?", (user_id, now_iso(), model_id))])
    return {**db.one("select * from model_versions where id=?", (model_id,)), "gate": "passed: beats best baseline on the holdout"}

# ===== FUNCTION: predict_lead_time() =====
# ID: F0536 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/scinsight/learning.py:88-98
# ROLE: Prediction with the PROMOTED configuration: re-fit deterministically on all receipts (no pickled model files) and predict
#       the lead time for a supplier / quantity / order date.
# INPUTS:
#   db: Database, tenant: str, model_row: dict (promoted model_versions row), supplier_id: str, quantity: float, on: date.
# OUTPUT:
#   float | None -> predicted days (1 decimal); None when the supplier was not in the model's feature set.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0332 Service.lead_time() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0418 Database (references)
#   -> F0532 _rows() (calls)
#   -> F0422 Database.one() (calls)
#   -> F0533 _features() (calls)
def predict_lead_time(db: Database, tenant: str, model_row: dict, supplier_id: str, quantity: float, on: date) -> float | None:
    """Re-fit the promoted configuration deterministically on all receipts and predict (no pickles: reproducible from data)."""
    rows = _rows(db, tenant)
    suppliers = json.loads(model_row["metrics"]).get("suppliers") or sorted({r["supplier_id"] for r in rows})
    if supplier_id not in suppliers:
        return None
    contract = db.one("select contract_lead_time_days from supplier_items where tenant_id=? and supplier_id=? order by material_id limit 1", (tenant, supplier_id))
    model = GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=150, max_depth=2, learning_rate=0.05, random_state=7)
    model.fit(_features(rows, suppliers), [r["lead"] for r in rows])
    # One synthetic feature row for the request.
    x = _features([{"supplier_id": supplier_id, "quantity": quantity, "order_date": on.isoformat(), "contract_lead_time_days": contract["contract_lead_time_days"]}], suppliers)
    return round(float(model.predict(x)[0]), 1)

# ROLE: Record a retraining REQUEST with evidence (verified learning records, their mean absolute error); training is separate.
# INPUTS:

#   -> F0416 now_iso() (calls)
def retraining_request(db: Database, tenant: str, user_id: str, reason: str) -> dict:
    verified = db.query("select * from learning_records where tenant_id=? and approved_for_training=1", (tenant,))
    rid = f"RR-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:10].upper()}"
    evidence = {"verified_learning_records": len(verified), "mean_abs_error_days": round(sum(r["abs_error"] for r in verified) / len(verified), 2) if verified else None}

    return {"id": rid, "status": "pending_human_approval", "evidence": evidence,
            "note": "A request only. Training runs on POST /api/v1/learning/train-lead-time-model by an MLOps engineer; promotion needs the director."}

    try:

    """Retrieve governed policy context (contracts, SOPs, quality and logistics policies) from PostgreSQL + pgvector."""

# ===== FUNCTION: _keyword_route() =====
# ID: F0543 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/agentflow.py:122-129
# ROLE: Deterministic route: request type from _regex_extract first, then the KEYWORDS table, default "director".
# INPUTS:
#   text: str.
# OUTPUT:
#   Route.
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0544 supervisor() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0588 _regex_extract() (calls)
def _keyword_route(text: str) -> Route:
    kind = _regex_extract(text).get("request_type")
    if kind == "factory_readiness":
        return "production"
    if kind == "stock_balance":
        return "warehouse"
    lower = text.lower()
    return next((route for route, words in KEYWORDS if any(w in lower for w in words)), "director")

# ===== FUNCTION: supervisor() =====
# ID: F0544 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/agentflow.py:132-144
# ROLE: Node 3: SAP-write guardrail first (deterministic), then the Qwen structured router, then the keyword fallback.
# INPUTS:
#   state.
# OUTPUT:
#   dict -> route, route_reason.
# CALLED BY:
#   (none found)
# CALLS:
#   -> F0538 AgentFlowState (references)
#   -> F0540 _last_human() (calls)
#   -> F0008 get_settings() (calls)
#   -> F0728 chat_model() (calls)
#   -> F0539 RouteDecision (references)
#   -> F0543 _keyword_route() (calls)
def supervisor(state: AgentFlowState) -> dict:
    text = _last_human(state)
    if WRITE_INTENT.search(text):
        return {"route": "boundary", "route_reason": "guardrail: SAP write intent"}
    settings = get_settings()
    if settings.llm_enabled:
        try:
            router = chat_model(settings, max_tokens=200).with_structured_output(RouteDecision, method="function_calling")
            decision = router.invoke([SystemMessage(content="Route supply-chain requests to the right business role. " + RouteDecision.__doc__), HumanMessage(content=text)])
            return {"route": decision.route, "route_reason": decision.reason or "llm"}
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            LLM_ERRORS.labels("langgraph_agentflow").inc()
    return {"route": _keyword_route(text), "route_reason": "keyword fallback"}

# ===== FUNCTION: _analysis_from() =====
# ID: F0547 · function · used
# ORIGINAL FILE: backend/app/agentflow.py:158-168
# ROLE: The newest tool result that is a stored analysis (analysis_id) of an allowed use case WITH proposed actions — the only thing
#       that may go to approval (quantities come from tool output, never from LLM text).
# INPUTS:
#   messages: list, use_cases: set[str].
# OUTPUT:
#   dict (empty when none).
# CALLED BY:
#   <- F0551 _specialist.node() (calls)
# CALLS:
#   (none found)
def _analysis_from(messages: list, use_cases: set[str]) -> dict:
    for message in reversed(messages):
        if not isinstance(message, ToolMessage):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(str(message.content))
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if isinstance(payload, dict) and payload.get("analysis_id") and payload.get("use_case") in use_cases and payload.get("proposed_actions"):
            return payload
    return {}
